prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop homepage comp for fcullmann.com, approximately 1440 × 1000 landscape

Primary request: Design a shippable, contemporary English-language personal software-engineer website that clearly reads as a usable browser page, not a flat poster. The visual metaphor is an engineer's field notebook and tabbed technical reference manual, expressed with editorial precision. The dominant centerpiece is a real JSON Formatter working specimen with an editable-looking input pane and formatted output pane.

Scene/backdrop: Full-bleed warm cloth-and-paper workspace in #EEEAE0. No browser chrome and no device frame. The page itself is the composition.

Structure and hierarchy:
1. A compact horizontal top navigation with a small precise wordmark "fcullmann", then links "Tools", "Projects", "Articles", "About", plus a restrained right-side utility action.
2. Below it, a wide open manual/notebook spread occupying most of the first viewport. The identity header reads "Florian Ullmann" and "Senior Software Engineer" with the line "Useful software, carefully made."
3. The tool specimen is dominant: clearly labeled "JSON Formatter", with a compact "Format JSON" action; two code-editor-like panes labeled "Input" and "Formatted output"; the input contains believable compact JSON and the output shows the same JSON correctly indented with readable syntax highlighting. Include practical micro-controls such as copy/clear only if visually restrained.
4. A visible stacked side index on the outer right edge with four physical tabs labeled verbatim: "Tools", "Projects", "Articles", "About".
5. At the bottom edge of the viewport, show the beginning of two real website sections: "Featured tools" with visible entries "JSON Formatter", "Base64", and "UUID Generator"; and "Latest writing" with one or two plausible article rows. These sections must look navigable and continue below the fold.

Style/medium: High-fidelity web product UI screenshot, highly resolved layout and typography, contemporary editorial web design. Interpret field notebooks through disciplined page folds, sewn cloth grain, paper layers, ruled annotations, section dividers, clipped index tabs, tiny graphite technical notes, and honest material edges. Keep every decorative cue subordinate to usability.

Composition/framing: Straight-on desktop viewport. Strong 12-column editorial grid. Generous but efficient spacing. Compact header, large manual spread, dominant JSON tool. Maintain obvious clickable affordances, form boundaries, text hierarchy, and alignment. The lower section begins before the crop so the page feels scrollable.

Typography: Crisp modern grotesk for navigation and interface labels, confident editorial serif only for the main name or section display if useful, clean monospace for JSON. All text must be legible, correctly spelled, and rendered verbatim where specified.

Color palette: warm cloth/paper #EEEAE0; deep green-black #14201D for primary type and structural surfaces; vermilion #EF5B3F for primary action and selected markers; sage #90A89F for secondary tabs and code accents; graphite gray annotations. Strong accessible contrast, no muddy beige-on-beige text.

Materials/textures: Tactile but restrained woven cloth, uncoated paper tooth, subtle fold and edge shadows, precise printed ink. No scrapbook whimsy.

Text (verbatim): "fcullmann"; "Tools"; "Projects"; "Articles"; "About"; "Florian Ullmann"; "Senior Software Engineer"; "Useful software, carefully made."; "JSON Formatter"; "Format JSON"; "Input"; "Formatted output"; "Featured tools"; "Base64"; "UUID Generator"; "Latest writing".

Constraints: The final image must clearly look like a functional desktop website UI with real navigation, interactive controls, a credible JSON input/output specimen, and content continuing below. The JSON formatter must be the visual and functional focal point. English only. Keep the four side index tabs plainly visible and readable.

Avoid: Bootstrap-style cards; card-grid-heavy SaaS layout; doodles or hand-drawn cartoons; fake portrait; fake metrics or testimonial stats; generic gradients; glassmorphism; device mockup; browser chrome; watermark; poster-only composition; illegible microtext; decorative notebook clutter; vintage steampunk styling; lorem ipsum; duplicate navigation; excessive rounded pills.
